rewritten_query:
WITH needed_weeks AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT d_week_seq
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_month_seq BETWEEN 1207 AND 1230
),
wss AS (
    SELECT d.d_week_seq,
           ss.ss_store_sk,
           s.s_store_name,
           s.s_store_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d.d_day_name='Sunday' THEN ss.ss_sales_price ELSE NULL END) sun_sales,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d.d_day_name='Monday' THEN ss.ss_sales_price ELSE NULL END) mon_sales,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d.d_day_name='Tuesday' THEN ss.ss_sales_price ELSE NULL END) tue_sales,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d.d_day_name='Wednesday' THEN ss.ss_sales_price ELSE NULL END) wed_sales,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d.d_day_name='Thursday' THEN ss.ss_sales_price ELSE NULL END) thu_sales,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d.d_day_name='Friday' THEN ss.ss_sales_price ELSE NULL END) fri_sales,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d.d_day_name='Saturday' THEN ss.ss_sales_price ELSE NULL END) sat_sales
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    JOIN needed_weeks nw ON nw.d_week_seq = d.d_week_seq
    JOIN store s ON s.s_store_sk = ss.ss_store_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_sales_price / ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 17*0.01 AND 37*0.01
      AND s.s_state IN ('GA','IL','IN','MT','NM','OH','OR','TX')
    GROUP BY d.d_week_seq, ss.ss_store_sk, s.s_store_name, s.s_store_id
)
SELECT y.s_store_name1,
       y.s_store_id1,
       y.d_week_seq1,
       y.sun_sales1 / x.sun_sales2,
       y.mon_sales1 / x.mon_sales2,
       y.tue_sales1 / x.tue_sales2,
       y.wed_sales1 / x.wed_sales2,
       y.thu_sales1 / x.thu_sales2,
       y.fri_sales1 / x.fri_sales2,
       y.sat_sales1 / x.sat_sales2
FROM (
    SELECT wss.s_store_name AS s_store_name1,
           wss.s_store_id AS s_store_id1,
           wss.d_week_seq AS d_week_seq1,
           wss.sun_sales AS sun_sales1,
           wss.mon_sales AS mon_sales1,
           wss.tue_sales AS tue_sales1,
           wss.wed_sales AS wed_sales1,
           wss.thu_sales AS thu_sales1,
           wss.fri_sales AS fri_sales1,
           wss.sat_sales AS sat_sales1
    FROM wss
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_week_seq = wss.d_week_seq
    WHERE d.d_month_seq BETWEEN 1207 AND 1218
) y
JOIN (
    SELECT wss.s_store_name AS s_store_name2,
           wss.s_store_id AS s_store_id2,
           wss.d_week_seq AS d_week_seq2,
           wss.sun_sales AS sun_sales2,
           wss.mon_sales AS mon_sales2,
           wss.tue_sales AS tue_sales2,
           wss.wed_sales AS wed_sales2,
           wss.thu_sales AS thu_sales2,
           wss.fri_sales AS fri_sales2,
           wss.sat_sales AS sat_sales2
    FROM wss
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_week_seq = wss.d_week_seq
    WHERE d.d_month_seq BETWEEN 1219 AND 1230
) x
ON y.s_store_id1 = x.s_store_id2
AND y.d_week_seq1 = x.d_week_seq2 - 52
ORDER BY y.s_store_name1, y.s_store_id1, y.d_week_seq1
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The CTE `wss` originally aggregates the entire `store_sales` table across ~200 years of weeks. A `needed_weeks` CTE restricts aggregation to only weeks having at least one date in the required 24-month range (d_month_seq 1207–1230). All dates of those weeks are retained, so full-week totals for boundary weeks remain identical.

The store state filter (s_state IN ...) was applied twice after aggregation in the y and x subqueries. It is pushed into the `wss` CTE before aggregation, reducing the number of stores aggregated (~26% reduction) and making the outer s_state filters redundant.

The `store` join was moved into the `wss` CTE, carrying s_store_name and s_store_id through the aggregation. This eliminates two redundant one-to-one store joins in the y and x subqueries, since store_sk is unique in the store table (102 rows).

Implicit comma joins were rewritten to explicit ANSI JOINs. The date_dim joins in y/x are preserved because they control row multiplication semantics (one row per day in each week within the month range) and must not be removed to keep the result equivalent.
Constants such as 17*0.01 and 37*0.01 and month boundaries (1207+11, 1207+12, 1207+23) are trivially folded by the optimizer; the BETWEEN date-month bounds are kept as-is for clarity.
